# ANALYSIS: Census.gov Housing Data Catalog Search

The catalog search returned 364 matches from 1,809 total datasets, indicating a reasonably targeted result set rather than a broad miss. The top results are current: Planning Database 2026 and 2025 vintages, followed by American Community Survey 2024 1-Year products. All returned datasets carry complete API endpoints and geography/variables documentation pointers. No credential requirement and read-only access to the catalog endpoint reduce operational risk.

## Structured Findings

**Coverage match:** The search returned housing-focused datasets across multiple geographies and collection methods. The Planning Database products (block group and tract level, 2025–2026) are current and offer sub-county granularity. ACS 1-Year Subject Tables (2024) provide detailed housing attributes. PUMS microdata (2024) enables custom tabulation but requires more sophisticated analysis.

**Recency:** The newest vintages in the result set are 2026 (Planning Database), which is forward-dated and likely represents projected or staged data. The most recent actual-year release visible is 2024 ACS. No 2025 ACS 1-Year is shown in the top 8, suggesting it may not yet be published.

**Vintage ordering anomaly:** The catalog is ordered "newest vintage first" per the tool report, yet the results show 2026, 2025, then 2024—a logical ordering that happens to align with recency. This is expected behavior and does not indicate a search problem.

**What this search does NOT establish:** These are catalog entries only. No row has been fetched; the actual variable names, data quality, or whether housing-specific fields (rent, occupancy, unit count, tenure) are present in each product remain unconfirmed. The geography.json and variables.json endpoints are pointers, not inspections. Only fetching one dataset (recommended: ACS 1-Year Subject Tables 2024) will confirm whether the variables needed for the operator's use case exist and are current.
